title: Reality Fracture Rare + Mythic Set Review
scale: Letter grades (A+ to F), plus 'build-around' and 'sideboard' tags

format.summary: A grindy, deep format where every pack offers several playable options and decks in the same color pair can be built very differently. Rares show up often and games go long, so you see many rares, but the true bombs are mostly mythics. Much of the power sits in heavily pipped gold cards, and splashing is viable via heartwood tokens, land cyclers, and the mana rock, though strong narrow payoffs keep it from becoming soup.
format.speed: Slow and grindy; few aggressive two-drops, games are decided on turn six and later, boards stall, and decking occasionally happens given self-mill.

colors.take: No stack of busted white bombs this time; Guiding Hydra is its best rare, and green-white can win going wide with token makers like Hexhaven Battalion.
Deep in surveil, card draw, and planeswalkers, with standouts Sphinx of False Conclusions, The Theorist, and Seasoned Cryomancer; double-blue three-drops need about 10-11 blue sources.
Supports grindy graveyard recursion, great removal, and strong wraths like Overwrite the Multiverse that punish stalled boards.
Has the top rare in Ajani Unrelenting plus Chandra, with non-combat damage payoffs for aggressive red-black.
Heartwood ramp, mana sinks, and value creatures like Simulacrum Shaper and Verdant Kraken shine; mono-green payoffs exist but need many forests.

mechanics.name: Activated abilities / mana sinks
mechanics.take: Overperformed because the slow format rewards having things to do with mana late.

mechanics.name: Empower Jace
mechanics.take: Drives planeswalker synergies, and cards like Repurposed Enforcer and Avatar make it threatening.

mechanics.name: Heartwood tokens
mechanics.take: Provide ramp, fixing for splashes, and artifact counts for payoffs like Craterclaw Colossus and Puppet Crafting.

mechanics.name: Surveil/scry
mechanics.take: The blue-white engine can surveil nearly every turn, powering Proctor and Denzilore.

mechanics.name: Prepared spells
mechanics.take: Add flexible value; some rares like Codie or Cruel Calculations need many prepared cards to shine.

mechanics.name: Self-mill
mechanics.take: Common enough to put lands in the graveyard, fuel Tarmogoyf and recursion, and occasionally deck players.

advice: Prioritize the dual lands highly because many gold cards have heavy color requirements.
Splashing a single-pip bomb is well supported via heartwoods, land cyclers, and mana rocks; Marc splashed in four of five drafts.
Value mana sinks and late-game abilities, since games go long.
Count sources for heavy pips: around 10-11 for double-blue three-drops and at least 12 for quadruple-colored cards.
Respect wraths like Overwrite the Multiverse when overextending into stalled boards.
Build-around rares like Codie or Germinate Recruits are fine to try, but only when the specific support is there.
